chapterName: Middle Republic: The First Punic War (264-241 BCE)

questions.question: What were the ships of Rome's final fleet, which carried no corvus, modelled on?
options: Greek triremes from Syracuse
Duilius's flagship from Mylae
The heavy ships of Ecnomus
Egyptian royal galleys
A fast captured blockade runner
questions.explanation: About 200 quinqueremes were built on the model of a fast captured blockade runner. With no corvus, Romans had to win as sailors.
questions.sourceQuote: About 200 quinqueremes were built at no cost to the state, modelled on a fast captured blockade runner.

questions.question: How did the Romans defeat Carthage's war elephants at Panormus in 251 BC?
options: By blocking the road with chained wagons
By digging hidden pits in the road
By showering them with javelins from old siege earthworks
By frightening them with burning pigs
By charging them with heavy cavalry
questions.explanation: Javelins from behind old earthworks panicked the elephants, which stampeded back through their own infantry. The Carthaginians then fled.
questions.sourceQuote: The Roman commander showered the beasts with javelins from behind old siege earthworks.

questions.question: Why did Rome's victory at Akragas fail to bring a breakthrough in Sicily? (select all that apply)
options: Sicily's rugged hills favoured defenders
Rome's army had been wiped out in the battle
Carthage's coastal towns could be supplied by sea
Syracuse turned against Rome again
Carthage's elephants held all the mountain passes
questions.explanation: The hilly terrain favoured defenders, and Carthage's fortified coastal towns could be resupplied by sea. Years of raids and sieges followed.

questions.question: What did a Roman consul attempt at Drepana in 249 BC, leading to Carthage's greatest naval victory of the war?
options: A landing behind Hamilcar's lines
A naval assault in a storm
A blockade using sunken ships
A siege with floating towers
A night surprise attack on the enemy fleet
questions.explanation: The consul tried a night surprise attack, but his ships scattered in the dark and were pinned against the shore. It was Carthage's greatest naval victory of the war.
questions.sourceQuote: A Roman consul then tried a night surprise attack on the enemy fleet at Drepana.

questions.question: When Carthage tried to recover Sardinia in 237 BC, what did Rome do?
options: It agreed to share the island
It ignored the move entirely
It demanded Carthage hand over Hamilcar
It called it an act of war and forced Carthage to give up Sardinia and Corsica
It invaded Africa a second time
questions.explanation: Rome cynically treated the move as an act of war, seized Sardinia and Corsica, and demanded 1,200 more talents. This fuelled Carthaginian resentment.
questions.sourceQuote: It forced Carthage to surrender Sardinia and Corsica and pay 1,200 more talents.

questions.question: Where did Hamilcar Barca lead his veterans in 237 BC to build a new power base?
options: Numidia
Corsica
Sardinia
Spain
Gaul
questions.explanation: Hamilcar took his veterans to Spain in 237 BC. Carthage had earlier crushed its own rebellious foreign soldiers with great savagery.
questions.sourceQuote: That year Hamilcar led his veterans to Spain to build a new power base.

questions.question: After Regulus took Tunis, why did Carthage keep fighting instead of making peace?
options: Egypt promised a large army
Its people rose up against the council
Regulus's peace terms were too harsh
Regulus refused to negotiate at all
Hamilcar Barca forbade it
questions.explanation: Carthage asked for peace, but Regulus demanded such harsh terms that it chose to fight on. Tunis lay just 16 km from Carthage.
questions.sourceQuote: Carthage asked for peace, but his terms were so harsh that it fought on.

questions.question: When a Greek king from Epirus fought both Rome and Carthage in the 270s BC, how did Carthage help Rome?
options: It sent war elephants to Italy
It once ferried Roman troops in its ships
It handed Rome the island of Corsica
It paid Rome's mercenaries for a year
It lent Rome its best admiral
questions.explanation: Carthage supplied Rome and once carried Roman troops in its ships. The two cities had signed treaties in 509, 348 and around 279 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: When a Greek king from Epirus, in north-western Greece, fought them both in the 270s BC, Carthage supplied Rome and once ferried Roman troops in its ships.

questions.question: What was the main tactical idea behind the corvus?
options: Shooting arrows from a high platform
Turning a sea battle into a land battle
Setting enemy ships on fire
Towing captured ships back to port
Ramming ships below the waterline
questions.explanation: The corvus pinned two ships together so Roman soldiers could charge across. That suited Rome's legions, which excelled at land fighting.
questions.sourceQuote: A sea battle became a land battle, the kind Rome's legions excelled at.

questions.question: With the Senate deadlocked over helping Messana, who finally decided to send Roman forces?
options: The chief priest after consulting omens
The Senate in a second vote
The two consuls acting alone
Rome's Italian allies
The popular assembly
questions.explanation: The question went to the popular assembly, which voted yes. One consul had urged war and promised rich plunder.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate (*senatus*) was deadlocked, so the question went to the popular assembly (*comitia*).
